stories.headline: United States and Canada pause 50 percent tariff threat after reaching trade deal
stories.body:
The United States and Canada have reached a temporary agreement to pause a major tariff threat against Canadian imports [c2, c6]. US President Donald Trump announced late on Tuesday on Truth Social that he paused proposed 50% tariffs against Canada for a three-day period [c6]. The new 50% US tariffs threatened by the administration would have covered approximately $20 billion worth of Canadian goods [c7].

Following the announcement, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer held a 45-minute meeting with his Canadian counterpart on Wednesday [c1]. Greer expressed optimism about the outcome of the discussions [c2]. He stated that officials feel confident they reached an agreement that will protect American workers, jobs, and supply chains while strengthening the North American economy [c2]. On Wednesday afternoon, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney met with his cabinet and Canadian provincial leaders to brief them on the trade deal [c3].

The pause comes after months of trade friction between the two neighboring nations. In February 2025, the White House hit Canada with a 25% tariff [c10]. US officials cited inadequate progress by Canada in curbing cross-border illegal immigration and drug trafficking as the reason for those tariffs [c10]. Trade between Canada and the United States is extensive, reaching an estimated $909 billion in 2024 according to the Office of the US Trade Representative [c11]. Canada is heavily reliant on this economic relationship, as nearly 72% of Canada's goods exports went to the United States last year [c8].

Canadian public opinion has shown strong support for standing firm against American economic pressure. A poll by the firm Leger found that 56% of surveyed Canadians want Canada to take a hardline approach in trade negotiations with the United States [c4]. Canadian authorities have previously taken direct action against US trade measures [c5]. Last year, most Canadian provinces imposed a ban on US alcohol sales in retaliation to US tariffs [c5]. Cross-border energy projects have also seen past cancellations [c9]. Owner TC Energy halted the 1,200-mile Keystone XL pipeline project in 2021 after US President Joe Biden revoked a key permit [c9].

vocab.meaning: a person holding a position that corresponds to another person in a different organization or country
an action taken to harm someone in return for harm they caused
officially canceled or took back a law, decision, or permit

stories.headline: Israeli military opens criminal probe after admitting forces shot at car carrying Hind Rajab
stories.body:
The Israeli military admitted on Wednesday that its troops opened fire in 2024 on a car carrying five-year-old Hind Rajab and six of her family members in Gaza [c12]. Hind Rajab died in January 2024 after making an emergency phone call to the Palestinian Red Crescent while trapped inside the vehicle [c15]. Palestine Red Crescent operator Rana Faqih stayed on the line for hours with the child while appealing to the Israeli army to allow an ambulance to reach her [c19].

A 2024 Al Jazeera investigation indicated an Israeli tank was likely 13 to 23 metres away from the vehicle [c17]. Research agency Forensic Architecture and Earshot mapped 335 bullet holes on the body of the car [c20]. Her story drew international attention, and the docudrama 'The Voice of Hind Rajab', directed by Kaouther Ben Hania, premiered at the 82nd Venice International Film Festival on September 3, 2025 [c16].

The Israel Defense Forces stated that it has been conducting intensive combat across numerous fronts in an exceptionally complex operational reality for more than a thousand days [c18]. In a separate decision, the IDF ordered a military police criminal investigation into the March 2025 killing of 15 Palestinian medics and humanitarian personnel near Rafah [c13]. However, the military decided not to open a criminal investigation into April 2024 airstrikes that killed seven World Central Kitchen aid workers [c14]. In June, a UN commission reported that Israeli forces have killed more than 20,000 children and injured 44,000 in Gaza since October 2023 [c21].

vocab.meaning: a dramatized television film or show based on real events
an official group of people given the power to investigate or perform a specific task

stories.headline: Helicopter crash in Kenya kills seven people including five American citizens
stories.body:
A Eurocopter EC130 B4 helicopter crashed in Samburu county, Kenya, at approximately 09:13 local time on Wednesday, killing all seven people on board [c22]. The crash occurred near Mount Ololokwe [c27]. Emergency teams from the Kenya Red Cross participated in a multiagency response effort at the site [c28]. Tropic Air Kenya dispatched two of its helicopters to assist in search and rescue operations [c27]. By Wednesday evening, three bodies remained trapped in the wreckage due to ongoing flames [c29].

A US State Department spokesperson confirmed that five of the seven people killed in the crash were US citizens [c25]. Among the victims was 55-year-old Jose Suarez, the president and general manager of several Telemundo stations in Florida [c26]. Ecuador's Strategic Intelligence Center Director General Michele Sensi-Contugi and his wife Stephany Hollihan were also killed in the incident [c23].

Helicopter crashes have previously claimed high-profile lives in the region. In April 2024, Kenyan military chief Gen Francis Omondi Ogolla died in an army helicopter crash in western Kenya [c24].

vocab.meaning: sent off to a destination for a specific purpose
involving or combining several different government or administrative agencies

stories.headline: Former Ukrainian defence minister calls for elections as official is dismissed in corruption probe
stories.body:
Former Ukrainian defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov posted a video on YouTube on Tuesday calling for wartime presidential elections in Ukraine [c30]. Fedorov was fired as defence minister in mid-July, just six months after his appointment [c36]. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed Yevhenii Khmara as the new defence minister following Fedorov's dismissal [c31]. Elections have been suspended in Ukraine under martial law, which has been in effect since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022 [c37].

Fedorov's call comes during ongoing government anti-corruption investigations. On Wednesday, Ukraine's deputy head of the presidential office Iryna Mudra was dismissed amid anti-corruption searches [c33]. Ukraine's anti-corruption agency NABU reported investigating a conspiracy involving the laundering of 150 million hryvnias through a state-owned bank to post bail for former energy minister Herman Haluschenko [c34]. In late 2025, former presidential chief aide Andriy Yermak resigned following a search of his home, and he was arrested in May on suspicion of money laundering [c35].

Meanwhile, violent fighting continues in the country. On Wednesday, a Russian drone strike hit a minibus in the southern city of Kherson, killing four people [c32].

vocab.meaning: temporary rule by military authorities during an emergency when civil law is suspended
a secret plan by a group of people to do something illegal or harmful

stories.headline: Pakistan summons US diplomat after ambassador calls Jammu and Kashmir an important part of India
stories.body:
Pakistan's Foreign Ministry summoned the US Charge d'Affaires in Islamabad on Wednesday to lodge a formal demarche [c38]. The diplomatic protest came after US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor made statements during a visit to Srinagar [c38, c39]. While visiting the region, Ambassador Gor stated, "This is an important part of India and so I'm here visiting for the first time" [c39].

During his visit to Srinagar, Ambassador Gor met with Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah at the chief minister's official residence [c42]. The diplomatic visit and remarks drew quick reaction from Pakistani officials and local political leaders in the region [c41, c43]. Former Pakistan ambassador to the US Masood Khan criticized Gor's statements [c41]. Khan claimed that the remarks reflected a lack of understanding regarding the history of Jammu and Kashmir [c41].

Local leaders also raised issues regarding travel policies during the visit [c43]. PDP president Mehbooba Mufti called on Ambassador Gor on the social media platform X to review and withdraw the existing travel advisory for Kashmir [c43]. The United States currently maintains a Level 4 "do not travel" advisory for Jammu and Kashmir [c40].

vocab.meaning: a formal diplomatic representation or protest made by one government to another
an official announcement or warning giving advice on safety or travel

stories.headline: Fire at Kolkata hotel building leaves nine people dead including four Bangladeshi citizens
stories.body:
A major fire broke out at around 1:45 am on Wednesday in a five-storey building housing several hotels on Mirza Ghalib Street in Kolkata, killing nine people [c44]. West Bengal Fire and Emergency Services Minister Kaushik Chowdhury stated that firefighters saved around 80 lives during the blaze [c45]. Kolkata Police reported that 60 people were rescued from the hotel building [c46].

Four of the Bangladeshi nationals who died in the fire were identified as journalist Debashish Dutta, his wife Afsana Shimmin, their three-year-old son Sharnashish Dutta, and Md Akram Ali [c48].

The tragedy in Kolkata comes just days after another fatal hotel fire in the state. Two days prior to the Kolkata fire, a hotel fire in Tarapith, located in the Birbhum district, also killed nine people [c47].

vocab.meaning: citizens or subjects of a particular nation
an administrative area of a country or state

stories.headline: India and Palestine sign agreements to build hospital and vocational center in West Bank
stories.body:
Indian Ministry of External Affairs Secretary Sripriya Ranganathan visited Ramallah on Wednesday and met with Palestinian Prime Minister Mohammad Mustafa [c49]. During the visit, Indian and Palestinian officials signed two memoranda of understanding [c52]. The agreements cover the construction of a 200-bed hospital in Jenin and a Technical and Vocational Education and Training Centre [c52].

Following the agreements, Indian and Palestinian officials held a groundbreaking ceremony for the 200-bed super-speciality hospital in Arrabeh city, located in the Jenin Governorate [c50]. As part of the diplomatic mission, Sripriya Ranganathan handed over a consignment of life-saving medicines, including anti-cancer drugs, to the Palestinian health ministry [c53].

In New Delhi, Palestinian Ambassador to India Abdullah M. Abu Shawesh held a press conference at the Palestinian embassy on Wednesday to discuss the developments [c51].

vocab.meaning: official written agreements or statements setting out rules or terms
a batch of goods or materials delivered to someone

stories.headline: Court sends former Delhi minister Satyendar Jain to 14-day judicial custody in corruption case
stories.body:
The Rouse Avenue Court remanded former Delhi minister Satyendar Jain and four other accused individuals to 14 days of judicial custody on Wednesday [c54]. The court order was issued in connection with an ongoing corruption investigation involving the Delhi Jal Board [c54]. In the same court proceeding, accused DJB employee Ankit Shrivastava was remanded to two days of Anti-Corruption Branch custody [c55].

The arrests occurred a day prior to the court ruling. On Tuesday, the Anti-Corruption Branch arrested former Delhi Jal Board Chief Executive Officer Udit Prakash Rai along with Satyendar Jain and four others [c57]. The Anti-Corruption Branch alleged that Udit Prakash Rai and his family received Rs 1.52 crore in bribes linked to sewage treatment plant tenders [c58].

The legal actions triggered political responses in the capital. AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal alleged that Union Home Minister Amit Shah directly ordered the arrest of Satyendar Jain [c56].

vocab.meaning: sent an accused person back into custody while awaiting trial or further court orders
formal offers or bids to supply goods or execute work for a specific price
